_doc: Curated reading of the PDF B.2.4 ledger cells (version 2). `clauses` lists EVERY key-position, night-position, first-on-field and left-or-moved clause of the 44 ledger rows (history/arrivals.json, raw cells): each is transcribed (a gazetteer place or road, a time as printed or a labelled named-period convention, units, tier, the row's source keys as printed) or unresolved with its reason. `approach`, `positions`, `activities` and `departures` are the entries that drive geometry and events; each names its clause. Every phrase is literally in its ledger cell (the loader refuses one that is not); no entry is a coordinate. A clause the record cannot place is left unresolved, never guessed.

named_periods.note: Labelled conventions, not historical claims: PDF B.2.2 defines [NIGHT] as after the end of civil twilight (20:04) and [DUSK] as sunset 19:32 to 20:04 from the computed July 2 values (it prints sunset 19:32 for Jul 1 too). Applied to the date a clause prints; a night position is held from the start of the night.

conventions.scope: A clause belongs to the unit of its ledger row and everything under it unless it names a narrower roster unit; a unit never takes a clause that falls before its own ledger gate (Q04); a nearer clause replaces a farther one within 90 minutes; a clause at the place a unit already stands changes nothing.
conventions.window: The start of a printed window is the time of the place; a movement window ("advance to", "retreat to", "sent to") departs at the start and arrives at the end; a clause with only a date is recorded and not scheduled.
conventions.activity_clips: The ledger names an activity in words; the clip is the renderer's: works/digging/wall-building = build_works, camp/bivouac = camp, rests = rest, halts = halt, steps off/marches/countermarch/advance = march, attack/assault/counterattack/charge = double_quick (foot) or gallop (mounted), guns open = serve_guns, hold/do not advance = stand. Plausible-procedural.
